Seamaster Diver 300M

Dive · 41–42mm · 300m · automatic · 1993–2026

The Omega Seamaster Diver 300M is a professional dive watch known for its robust build, 300-meter water resistance, and distinctive design cues like a helium escape valve at 10 o'clock, skeletonized hands, and often a wave-patterned dial.

The story

Launched in 1993, the Seamaster Diver 300M quickly gained iconic status after its appearance on the wrist of James Bond in the 1995 film *GoldenEye*. The first generation featured an aluminum bezel and a distinctive wave pattern on the dial. A significant technical evolution occurred with the introduction of Omega's Co-Axial escapement in the Calibre 2500, enhancing the movement's long-term performance. Around 2012, the design was updated with a ceramic bezel and a glossy lacquered dial, temporarily removing the signature wave motif. In 2018, for the model's 25th anniversary, the Diver 300M was comprehensively redesigned, reintroducing a laser-engraved wave pattern on a ceramic dial, increasing the case size to 42mm, and incorporating the advanced in-house Master Chronometer Calibre 8800.
